title: Walmart (WMT) Reverses Course On In Store Digital Wallet Payments
detail:
Walmart (WMT) Reverses Course On In Store Digital Wallet Payments
Bailey Pemberton
Tue, September 22, 2026 at 2:14 PM EDT 2 min read
WMT
Trade Walmart on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Walmart (NasdaqGS:WMT) is rolling out support for Apple Pay and Google Pay across its U.S. stores in a policy reversal.

The retailer previously promoted its own Walmart Pay solution and had limited acceptance of third party digital wallets in stores.

Apple Pay and Google Pay support is expected to cover in person checkout, with timing and specific rollout details still emerging.

Walmart's move to support Apple Pay and Google Pay matters, but investors also need to think beyond this payments shift. We have also flagged 2 other big wins for Walmart.

For readers interested in more ways digital infrastructure can shape retail and commerce, a natural next step is 86 AI infrastructure stocks.

NasdaqGS:WMT Earnings & Revenue Growth as at Sep 2026

Walmart operates a global network of retail and wholesale stores, membership clubs, ecommerce sites, and mobile apps, so its decision on which digital wallets to accept affects how millions of shoppers pay at checkout. That reach gives any shift in payment options real weight for how transactions flow across the wider Consumer Retailing industry.

How Walmart's Apple Pay and Google Pay shift pressures its "alternate profit pools" story

The Walmart Narrative leans on digital commerce and higher-margin services to justify the effort going into omnichannel payments, data, and membership. This wallet reversal plugs straight into that story because it trades some control at checkout for potentially richer data and more ways to keep shoppers inside Walmart's ecosystem.

Diversification into higher-margin streams and international expansion strengthens earnings resilience and transforms Walmart's profit mix beyond traditional retail...

See how the full story points towards a $128 fair value for Walmart.

Support for Apple Pay and Google Pay clearly feeds the catalyst that omni-channel experiences and rapid delivery keep customers loyal to Walmart rather than to Amazon or Target. Easier tap-to-pay on phones can tighten the loop between physical stores, Walmart's apps, and services like Walmart+, which the Narrative treats as important higher-margin streams.

The move also brushes against a flagged risk that digital growth brings heavier logistics and tech spending without enough payback. Handing payment "front door" access to Apple and Alphabet could make it harder for Walmart Connect and marketplace services to fully monetise shopper data if those partners capture more of the relationship.

For you as an investor, this wallet news only really matters in the context of whether you buy into Walmart's broader story about digital ecosystems and alternate profit pools reshaping the business over time.

title: Dollar General's Project Renovate and Elevate Drive Comp Sales Lift
detail:
Dollar General's Project Renovate and Elevate Drive Comp Sales Lift
Zacks Equity Research
Tue, September 22, 2026 at 12:00 PM EDT 3 min read
DG
WMT
TGT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Dollar General Corporation DG continues to enhance its overall retail network execution by making strategic capital investments in its existing store footprint. Through two core store remodel initiatives — Project Renovate and Project Elevate — the retail chain is effectively unlocking higher productivity and strong same-store sales growth across its mature store base.

Project Renovate is the company's traditional full-remodel program, generally aimed at stores that are at least seven years removed from opening or their last major remodel. The work can include adding or replacing coolers and upgrading the location to Dollar General's latest store format. Project Elevate targets stores that are not yet old enough for a full remodel but still offer room for improvement. Project Elevate touches as much as 80% of a store through asset upgrades, merchandising changes, product adjacency adjustments and category refreshes.

The company continues to target an annualized comparable-sales lift of about 6% for Project Renovate stores and about 3% for Project Elevate locations. Through the end of the second quarter of fiscal 2026, Dollar General had completed 1,324 Project Renovate remodels and 1,422 Project Elevate remodels.

Dollar General still expects to complete about 2,000 Renovate projects and 2,250 Elevate projects for the full year. The two programs give the retailer a targeted way to extract additional sales from established stores while refreshing the shopping experience across different portions of its mature footprint.

How Walmart and Target Compare With DG on Store Remodels

Walmart Inc. WMT is also investing heavily in its physical store base, completing about 220 U.S. store remodels in the second quarter of fiscal 2027. Walmart U.S. comparable sales rose 2.6%, driven by higher transactions and unit volumes. Walmart said it continues investing in remodels and omni-enabling stores, supporting a store network that increasingly serves both in-store shoppers and e-commerce fulfillment.

Target Corporation TGT is seeing a clear response to store investment, with management citing reliable guest lifts after remodels. Target has more than 100 full-store remodels underway toward roughly 130 for the year. Target's comparable store sales increased 2.7% in the quarter. Target also said these remodels help bring its latest merchandising and experience improvements across the chain, reinforcing the role of refreshed stores in driving guest engagement.

Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT), the retail and digital-marketplace giant, received a bipartisan push for Federal Trade Commission scrutiny of its Sparky shopping assistant. Shares gained approximately 0.5% to $107.265, based on the latest quoted price, putting the stock 3.02% above its GF Value estimate of $104.12.

WMT GF Value chart
Walmart Gains as Sparky Draws an FTC Probe Request · us.finance.gurufocus

Senators Tammy Baldwin and Rick Scott want regulators to examine whether Sparky reliably helps shoppers identify American-made goods and whether potentially questionable country-of-origin claims are clearly surfaced. The request itself is not an FTC ruling, enforcement action or determination that Walmart broke the law. But it puts another spotlight on a fast-emerging issue: once AI starts steering purchasing decisions, the quality of the product data behind those recommendations matters just as much as the chatbot interface.

That is where the investment angle gets interesting. Better seller documentation and more structured origin data could raise compliance costs, but they could also make Walmart's marketplace more trustworthy and its AI assistant more useful. The valuation picture remains relatively balanced: the stock is only 3.02% above GF Value, suggesting investors are paying a modest premium rather than pricing in a huge gap. Sparky can become a conversion engine, but Walmart now has to prove that smarter shopping recommendations can scale without creating a bigger verification headache.

title: Has The Price For Amazon Stock Already Peaked?
detail:
Has The Price For Amazon Stock Already Peaked?
Trefis Team
Mon, September 21, 2026 at 4:43 PM EDT 4 min read
AMZN
SPGI
META
GOOG
MSFT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

The market has rewarded this tech giant for its powerful business engine, but a recent pullback forces investors to ask if the best part of the run is already over.

Amazon.com (AMZN) is a business of two giants. One delivers packages to your door. The other, AWS, delivers the cloud computing power that runs a huge portion of the modern internet. The market has long rewarded this combination, placing the stock in the top 36% of large US stocks for trend strength. But the tape tells a more complicated story right now.

The stock has pulled back about 5% from its one-month high and trades about 11% below its 52-week high. Over the last year, it underperformed the wider market; while the S&P 500 (SPY) returned +16.8%, Amazon shares returned just +9.5%. This sets up the essential momentum question for any would-be buyer: is this a pause in a quality-fueled run, or has the price already charged for all the good news?

Is There a Real Engine Behind the Momentum?

The fundamental thesis for Amazon stock is supported by sustained expansion in its most profitable division. AWS revenue growth hit 37% year-over-year in the last quarter, a pace management noted was its fastest in 18 quarters. The cloud unit is now a $169 billion annualized revenue run rate business. This is the core of the bull case. Company-wide, revenue over the last twelve months grew 15.8%, nearly double the S&P 500 median revenue growth of 8.3%.

This growth, however, comes at a cost. The company's operating margin over the last twelve months is 12.1%, which trails the S&P 500 median of 18.6%. This reflects the immense investment required to stay ahead, particularly in the artificial intelligence arms race. Management is betting that this spending will cement its leadership for the next decade.

What Does a Share of This Growth Cost Today?

Despite its powerful growth profile, Amazon's stock doesn't carry an extreme premium versus the market. It trades at a price-to-earnings multiple of 20.2, which is actually below the S&P 500 median of 22.5.

The stock also remains about 11% below its two-year high of $284.02, suggesting the market is not in a state of pure euphoria. The price-to-sales multiple of 3.5 is slightly higher than the S&P 500 median of 3.1, but not dramatically so.

The real price of admission, however, is the risk embedded in the company's strategy. The central question, as one recent analysis asks, is whether the AI capex surge is a threat to Amazon stock. Management now expects to spend approximately $220 billion on capital expenditures in 2026, a huge sum driven largely by the build-out of data centers for AWS and AI. The risk is that this large investment cycle, vulnerable to cost inflation, could fail to generate the high returns shareholders expect, pressuring cash flow for years to come.

title: Takeaways for banks from Walmart's about-face on Apple and Google wallets
detail:
Takeaways for banks from Walmart's about-face on Apple and Google wallets
Cheryl Winokur Munk
Mon, September 21, 2026 at 12:31 PM EDT 6 min read
WMT
AAPL
GOOG
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Key insights: Walmart is supporting Apple Pay after a long holdout, creating new opportunities for banks and payment companies.

What's at stake: The move resulted from a shift in consumer preference for more digital options.

Expert quote: "Even a retailer with the scale to promote its own payment experience has recognized the value of accepting the methods customers already use. Banks, merchants, and payment providers that fail to support those preferences risk losing transaction volume and everyday relevance," —Ed Dean, Nuvei.

There is a broader urgency around immediate fund availability in consumers' day-to-day financial lives.

Walmart's change of heart regarding Apple Pay and Google Pay acceptance is a major coup for mobile wallets. For banks, it's also a wake-up call.

Recent research from payments software company Nuvei found that 57% of respondents feel meaningful differences between payment methods and expect to find the one they prefer waiting for them. Mobile wallets are one of those payment methods, with more web-based and in-person businesses asking for Apple Pay and Google Pay, according to Eric Cohen, chief executive of Merchant Advocate, a merchant services consulting firm. "Banks can't fight this movement," he told American Banker.

Here are several lessons banks can glean from Walmart's latest move:

The shift is customer-driven

Walmart's shift ultimately reflects consumer preference, Ed Dean, vice president of product at Nuvei, said in an email. "Even a retailer with the scale to promote its own payment experience has recognized the value of accepting the methods customers already use. Banks, merchants, and payment providers that fail to support those preferences risk losing transaction volume and everyday relevance."

Owning the account isn't owning the relationship

Banks may still be holding on as a customer's primary financial institution, but the attack is actually happening on payment primacy, Prashant Shah, vice president of product management at SoFi Tech Solutions, said in an email. The financial technology company's transaction data reinforces the shift: Tap-to-pay gained more share than any other payment method in the second quarter, and Walmart, the biggest holdout until now, will be a game-changer.

"If your card isn't the one the customer is actually using, you're losing spend and interchange to another issuer, even if that customer still keeps their checking account with you," Shah said. "Over time, you can end up being where the paycheck lands, but not the card they reach for."
